diagram_candidates.rationale: The theorem centers on the Smith–Volterra–Cantor construction: at each stage every retained interval is split into two closed pieces by removing an open middle interval, yielding a compact perfect nowhere dense set with positive interval-cover lower bound. A small stage-by-stage diagram can make the retained pieces and deleted gaps immediately legible and distinguish this fat construction from the ordinary middle-thirds Cantor set. This is a high-value teaching candidate, not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.stage_sets: S_n is the union of N_n=2^n closed intervals [e_j^(n),e_j^(n)+lambda_n] in [0,1], and S is their nested intersection.
concrete_maps_and_relations.sizes: lambda_(n+1)<g_n, lambda_n=g_n+lambda_(n+1), and each gap has length g_n-lambda_(n+1)=4^(-n-1); with 2^n gaps at stage n, total deleted length is 2^(-n-2).

diagram_candidates.rationale: The theorem defines a compact solid between two continuous graph maps and identifies its integral with integration over vertical fibres. A schematic cross-section would make the geometric set and the section map in the formula immediately legible.
